M8-03-DEBTSCHEDULE.6:
## Debt schedule

Senior debt at closing: {p0}, at {p1}. The contract provides for mandatory amortisation of {p2} a year and a **cash sweep** of {p3}: that share of excess cash must go to prepayment.

Order matters: CFADS pays interest first (on opening debt), then mandatory amortisation; what's left is excess cash, and only part of that goes into the sweep.

Build the four rows of the schedule, one formula per row copied across the three years. Opening debt is already linked to the previous year's closing debt.

M8-07-VALUEBRIDGE.2:
Build the **Value Creation Bridge** to explain to investors where the LBO return came from.

Entry vs Exit parameters:
- **EBITDA**: from {p0} (Entry) to {p1} (Exit)
- **EV/EBITDA multiple**: from {p2} (Entry) to {p3} (Exit)
- **Net Debt**: reduced from {p4} (Entry) to {p5} (Exit)

The increase in equity value splits into three effects that, added together, must give exactly the change in equity:

- **EBITDA growth**, valued at the entry multiple (so the change in multiple isn't counted twice);
- **change in multiple**, applied to exit EBITDA;
- **deleveraging**: net debt repaid with the cash generated becomes value for shareholders.

Compute the three effects, then the change in equity directly from the entry and exit values: if the bridge doesn't reconcile, one of the three effects is wrong.
M8-07-VALUEBRIDGE.18: In {B_EFF_GROWTH} the effect of EBITDA growth, valued at the entry multiple.
M8-07-VALUEBRIDGE.19: In {B_EFF_MULT} the effect of the change in multiple, on exit EBITDA.
M8-07-VALUEBRIDGE.21: In {B_DELTA_EQ} the change in equity calculated directly: exit equity minus entry equity, each as EV minus net debt. It must match the bridge total.
M8-07-VALUEBRIDGE.22: =B8-B9: the debt that's no longer there.
M8-07-VALUEBRIDGE.title: Value creation bridge: splitting EBITDA, multiples and deleveraging

Waiting makes MoIC grow, but IRR measures the return **per year**: a higher MoIC obtained over more time can be worth less. The fund, which has to return capital to investors and raise new money, looks above all at IRR.

Compute the IRR of the three scenarios and have the sheet point out the best one.

M8-11-RETURNSATTRIBUTION.2:
Build the full closing **Returns Waterfall** of the LBO.

Exit data:
- **Exit EBITDA**: {p0} at a {p1} multiple (Enterprise Value {p2})
- **Remaining Net Debt**: {p3}
- **Mezzanine Equity Kicker**: {p4} of gross Equity
- **Management Incentive Plan (MIP)**: {p5} of gross Equity
- **Sponsor Initial Entry Equity**: {p6}

At exit the gross equity doesn't all go to the sponsor: first the mezzanine collects its **equity kicker** (a share of the value, compensation for its subordinated risk), then management its **MIP** share. What's left is the sponsor's net return: the number that matters to the fund.

Walk down the waterfall: gross equity, the two shares, the sponsor's net equity and its net MoIC.
M8-11-RETURNSATTRIBUTION.20: In {B_GROSS_EQ} the gross equity at exit.
M8-11-RETURNSATTRIBUTION.21: In {C_MEZZ_VAL} what the mezzanine collects with its equity kicker.
M8-11-RETURNSATTRIBUTION.22: In {C_MGT_VAL} what management collects with the MIP.
M8-11-RETURNSATTRIBUTION.23: In {B_SPONSOR_NET} the equity left to the sponsor at the bottom of the waterfall.
M8-11-RETURNSATTRIBUTION.title: Returns attribution: the full LBO returns waterfall
